newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mostly lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were seen opening mostly lower Tuesday, except for gold which was expected to recover a little of the ground lost in Monday's sharp fall, but a firmer dollar in the past couple of days and steadier world stockmarkets would limit gold's gains, traders said.
COMEX December gold was seen opening unchanged to up 50 cents an ounce from Monday's close at $324.70 an ounce, after trading a $324.50-325/20 range in overnight ACCESS trade.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $322.50/40 early, compared to the London Tuesday morning fix at $322.10 and the New York close Monday around $321.10/60 an ounce.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks were unchanged Monday at 922,218 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks fell 152,949 ounces to 165,243,018 ounces.
COMEX September silver was seen opening unchanged to down 0.30 cent an ounce from Monday's close at $4.502.

NYMEX October platinum was expected to open down $1.00 to $2.00 an ounce from Monday's close at $416.40, while NYMEX September palladium was also seen opening down $1.00 to $2.00 from the previous close at $203.50.
Overnight TOCOM platinum and palladium prices slipped a little lower, but the physical market remains tight, traders said.
